# <span id="aanchor381"></span> Business Month Editor

The Current Business Month is usually defined as the open production month currently being processed. The business month is used in areas of such as PPAs. This business month concept also allows users to explicitly set the current business month for a given system within the application. By explicitly setting a business month, there could be one or more open production months, but the user has control over which month is the current business month. In addition, some data has the current business month recorded as part of the audit trail.

Each FLOWCAL system is set to use an explicit business month. For liquid meters, Tickets now have an explicitly recorded Business Month as part of the audit trail. Tickets that belong to a Location use the Location's System to establish the Business Month. Standalone tickets or tickets that do not belong to a Location do not have a Business Month.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Business Month Editor:

Go to **Setup** \> **Business Month**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 419;height: 143;" />

An application administrator must initially set the current business month. After the initial setup, any user with Meter Close privileges can set the business month. Once set, the business month may only be incremented by one month, every ten days.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Business Month Editor Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Business Month Editor:

- **Use the First Open Month** - Use the first open month as the Current Business Month.
- **Use the Business Month** - Use the specified business month as the Current Business Month.

</div>
